title: Best Chess Edit Explained
transcript: You have seen this position before in what is being called the best chess edit ever made. But, did you understand the sense behind every move that you saw? Well, if you didn't, [music] I am here to explain it to you. The truth of the matter is that in this position white is winning pretty much regardless of what is played. But, there is an opportunity of playing something absolutely incredible. After rook to B1 check, the black king moves to the side to step out of the attack. And this is where the first brilliant move of this position comes into play. The incredible queen to E4, an incredible move which, unfortunately, sacrifices the queen to the black army. But, whenever there is a knight so close to your opponent's king, you have to be looking for forks. And it just so happens that knight to D6 is a check, but also attacks every [music] other piece in the position of black. The king has to move, of [music] course, but there is only one square available, the D8 square, which allows to start collecting the pieces with a discovered check from the rook, forcing the king back to E8. This is the only move. But, of course, from E8, the black king can be checked again. And now, >> [music] >> with this pattern, the white knight is going to be able to keep checking the black king, keep attacking all of these pieces, and whenever the king moves, he's [music] going to give another check with the rook. And that is how white collects every single piece in the position of black. This position might not be the most incredible ever composed, but it sure is spectacular.
